newsitem.title: USA: Mariah Carey leads American Music Awards nominations.
newsitem.headline: Mariah Carey leads American Music Awards nominations.

text.p: Pop singer Mariah Carey grabbed five American Music Awards nominations, while 11 artists trailed with two nods each, organisers said on Wednesday.

The nominations are sweet revenge for Carey who was snubbed at the Grammy Awards earlier this year. She was nominated for favourite female artist in the pop/rock and soul/r&b categories, while her latest release, "Daydream," is a contender in the album section for both those categories. Additionally, she competes with Celine Dion and Whitney Houston for favourite adult contemporary artist.

However, as with the Grammys, a handful of American Music Awards nominations does not necessarily mean success on awards night. Last year, Hootie and the Blowfish and Boyz II Men led the pack with five nominations each. They went home with one and two awards respectively.

The awards will be handed out on Jan. 27 at Los Angeles' Shrine Auditorium, and the event will be screened that night on ABC. The list of nominees is compiled from sales and airplay data, and the night's winners are picked by a poll of 20,000 randomly chosen members of the public, whose tastes have traditionally favoured middle-of-the-road acts.
With two nominations each are: Toni Braxton, Garth Brooks, D'Angelo, Dion, Fugees, Alanis Morissette, the Smashing Pumpkins, Stone Temple Pilots, George Strait, Keith Sweat and Shania Twain.

The awards, now in their 24th year, have dropped the favourite artist of the year category after Garth Brooks refused to accept the award at the last ceremony. The country star said Hootie and the Blowfish should have got it because they were bigger sellers last year.

Sources close to the organisers said Alanis Morissette would have been a shoo-in for the award this year, but it would have looked incongruous since her mega-selling release "Jagged Little Pill" has now been in the shops for almost 18 months and is still in the top 10. More recent releases by bigger name artists have paled by comparison in a bleak year for the music industry.
